summary:
We developed a tool for planning Lunar missions. It allows the user to see areas (or specific sites) and their Line of Sight to Earth and the Sun. It also allows the user to "land" on the moon and walk around, to see the sun rise over the horizon. This visual presentation can also be delivered in a more stylized mode, where the information is presented more clearly. It can also measure the suitability of a given site over a simulated 30-day period.

This is important because missions on the moon are dependent on Line of Sight to Earth for communications, and are heavily affected by being within LoS to the Sun or not. The tool makes it easy to test around and visualize different ideas, set at any given date - or a specific suitable date that the tool proposes.
details: The project is made in Unity and coded mostly in C#. It's main benefits are the ease of use, the customization options as to what to show on screen, and the visualization of the information needed. The main limiting factor was calculation power - having the real distances and sizes of the Sun, the Earth and the Moon was simply not possible, and there was not time to put together a program which segmentially loads information as it is needed - so this compromise was used instead, putting the moon in the system's center and representations of the Earth and the Sun are then used to provide the same data and visualizations.
